comments.content: loadWorkspaceFromDb calls `handleCommandError(e, "workspace_load", { silent: true })` and *also* returns `{ ok: false, error }`. The caller is supposed to surface the failure on its own — but the `silent: true` flag suggests handleCommandError already shows a notification. If the caller additionally toasts, users see the same failure twice; if they don't, the failure is silent *and* the return value is unused. Either drop the `handleCommandError` call (let the caller decide everything from `{ok:false,error}`) or drop the `{ok:false}` return and document that handleCommandError is the sole UX channel.

Path regex can over‑match: the space‑allowing branch (`PATH_CHAR_SPACE*?` … known extension) has no left token boundary and permits spaces and most ASCII punctuation, so a token can start inside a larger word (e.g. `foo/home/user/a.pdf`) and the space‑allowing branch can swallow ordinary prose until a later whitelisted extension. This can still produce the “Program”/wrong‑path problem the comment claims to fix. Consider adding a left boundary (look‑behind or explicit preceding whitespace/start) and constraining `PATH_CHAR_SPACE` so it cannot run across sentence punctuation.

URL branch keeps Markdown link delimiters such as a trailing `)` or `]`. The capture group excludes `< > " '` and full‑width punctuation but not ASCII parentheses/brackets, while `normalizeUrl` only strips `[.,;:!?]+$`. As a result `[label](https://example.com)` yields the URL `https://example.com)` which is opened verbatim. Either extend the URL character class to exclude trailing `)]` (or a balanced pair) or have the normalizer strip the closing bracket/parenthesis when it follows an URL scheme.

Bare‑domain regex mis‑classifies ordinary dotted filenames as URLs. `BARE_DOMAIN_RE` accepts any sequence of labels ending in a 2+‑letter TLD (e.g. `notes.md`, `report.pdf`, `foo.js`), so `normalizeUrl` prefixes `https://` and forwards it to `openUrl` instead of treating it as a (relative) file target. Tighten the pattern (require a slash/path, or reject known file extensions / numeric labels) and/or detect the domain in context before normalizing.
comments.existing_code:
/** 裸域名（www.example.com / example.com/path）：补 https:// 后可开 */
const BARE_DOMAIN_RE = /^(?:[a-z0-9-]+\.)+[a-z]{2,}(?:[/?#]|$)/i;

comments.content: Hard‑coded path allow‑lists are too narrow. `FILE_EXTS` only covers a small set of generated document types (no `.docm`, `.pages`, `.heic`, etc.), and `PATH_PREFIX` lists only a handful of Unix roots (`/Users|/home|/var|/tmp|/Library|/Applications|/opt`). Paths like `/workspace/report.pages` are rejected outright, and spaced paths with unsupported extensions still get truncated at the first space (the original “Program” bug). Either extend the lists to cover the real output directories/file types you need to open, or fall back to a more permissive path extractor when the allow‑list fails.

Native prototype mutation lacks a runtime guard. The function deliberately mutates `Element.prototype` — which the project's own security rules prohibit — and is exported with no check that it is being called from a jsdom test suite. `src/test/setup.ts` shows the project deliberately keeps setup.ts free of global prototype patches and pushes them into per-suite helpers like this one, so the risk is bounded today, but if a non-test file ever imports `stubScrollNoop` (e.g. a refactor that pulls a shared util into `src/`), the patch becomes permanent for the whole process. Suggestion: assert at the top of the function, e.g. `if (typeof window === "undefined" || typeof Element === "undefined") return;` or `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "production") return;`, so accidental production use becomes a no-op rather than a silent global mutation.

Helper is not idempotent — repeated calls register redundant hook pairs. Each invocation of `stubScrollNoop()` registers a fresh `beforeEach`/`afterEach` pair with its own closure-captured `patched` array. If a test file calls it more than once (e.g. once at module scope and once inside a nested `describe`, or via a shared helper re-imported in multiple suites) every test fires multiple copies of both hooks, with the extra pairs short-circuiting on the truthy guard. The behavior is correct but wasteful, and makes failure analysis confusing (deletions come from a different closure than the install). Suggestion: gate registration with a module-level `let installed = false;` so the helper is a no-op on subsequent calls, or document the single-call invariant in the JSDoc.

Cleanup relies entirely on `afterEach` running — patches leak if it doesn't. The JSDoc claims "scoped polyfill: beforeEach installs, afterEach uninstalls," but vitest will skip `afterEach` if the previous `it` was marked `skip`/`todo` after the hook, if the suite bails out via `beforeAll`/`afterAll` failures, or if a thrown error happens during setup in some configurations. Because `patched` is a closure variable that only ever grows inside `beforeEach`, any leak is bounded to whatever was installed at the moment cleanup stopped — but subsequent suites in the same worker will inherit the polyfills, and the `Element.prototype[name]` truthy guard in the next `beforeEach` will then `continue`, so an unrelated test that wants to spy on `scrollTo` will find the no-op already present and will silently no-op itself. Suggestion: pair the install with a try/finally, or use `vi.stubGlobal` / a `Symbol`-keyed property that the test can opt out of, so cleanup is independent of vitest's hook ordering.

`delete` on a host-object prototype is a slow, deopt-prone operation. Even though `Object.defineProperty` here sets `configurable: true` (so `delete` succeeds), removing an own property from `Element.prototype` invalidates the hidden class for every existing and future `Element` instance across the whole test worker. In suites that render many elements (ChatPanel / WidgetApp), this can measurably slow down test runs and pollute later unrelated tests. The current design is acceptable for a small helper, but if this file becomes more widely used, prefer `Object.defineProperty(..., { value: originalRef })` snapshots so cleanup is a write instead of a delete — or scope the polyfill by reassigning the prototype slot to a captured original rather than deleting it.
comments.existing_code: delete (Element.prototype as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)[name];

comments.content: The validator checks only that the three required status booleans exist, but this return keeps every extra key from the stored object. `GraphPage` enumerates `status` with `Object.keys` and indexes `STATUS_LABELS`; a persisted key such as `constructor` or `__proto__` therefore passes validation and produces a function/object as a React child, crashing the graph (other unknown keys create blank chips). Normalize the object to only the validated keys rather than returning the parsed object unchanged.

Swallowing a failed `setItem` does not provide the claimed session-only fallback: all getters read storage again, so a quota/security failure leaves them returning the old/default value. In particular, a preference changed while the settings page replaces the unmounted graph may never affect the next graph opening. Cache the intended value in memory when persistence fails (and clear that cache on invalidation), or return a failure result so callers can report that the setting was not retained.

`fallback` is used only when the key is absent; every malformed stored value is interpreted as `false`. Thus a corrupted/legacy value for `autoLayout` silently overrides its default of `true`. Accept only the two persisted encodings and fall back for every other value.

Implicit `any` on `assetsInlineLimit` predicate: the `(filePath) =>` parameter has no type annotation, so under a strict tsconfig it falls back to `any` (or fails to compile). Per project rules `any` must be avoided — type the parameter explicitly (e.g. `(filePath: string) => boolean | undefined`).

Case-sensitive `.svg` check: `filePath.endsWith(".svg")` only matches lowercase; any `.SVG`, `.Svg`, etc. will still be inlined into the main chunk and re-introduce the very bundle-bloat the comment is trying to prevent. Normalise the check (e.g. `filePath.toLowerCase().endsWith(".svg")`).

comments.content: localStorage shim implements only length/clear/getItem/key/removeItem/setItem but is typed as the full Storage interface (forEach, keys(), values(), entries(), [Symbol.iterator] are required by current lib.dom). Any production code that iterates storage (e.g., for...of over `localStorage`, `localStorage.forEach`, `localStorage.keys()`) will throw `TypeError: ... is not a function` at test time, producing silent test-coverage gaps. Add the missing methods (entries/keys/values returning IterableIterator via the same store, a forEach that delegates, and a [Symbol.iterator] that yields entries()).

The `key()` accessor rebuilds `Array.from(store.keys())` on every call, making it O(n) per invocation. Combined with the missing iteration APIs above, callers using `for (let i = 0; i < localStorage.length; i++) localStorage.key(i)` get quadratic behavior. Cache the key array and invalidate on mutations (setItem/removeItem/clear), or expose keys() and have callers use that instead.

comments.content: WebGL2RenderingContext / WebGLRenderingContext are stubbed as bare constructor functions with empty prototypes. The comment assumes only `typeof`/construction checks occur at module load, but if sigma (or any other unmocked module) reads static properties, accesses `WebGL2RenderingContext.prototype`, or calls any instance method (e.g., `getContextAttributes`, `createBuffer`), the import path will throw and the test will fail with a confusing stack trace pointing at the WebGL stub. Either guard with a more accurate feature-detect stub that returns a no-op object, or document which modules are safe to import.

crypto.randomUUID fallback uses `Math.random()` + `Date.now()`, which is non-deterministic and timing-dependent. Tests that capture the generated id (for equality, map keys, snapshot, or as a React key driving reconciliation) will flake across runs and especially when two UUIDs are generated in the same millisecond with overlapping random suffixes. Prefer a monotonic counter (`let n = 0; () => \`uuid-${++n}\``) — tests stay deterministic and reproducible.

The console.error spy uses `/not wrapped in act\(/` to swallow React 19 act() warnings, but the same suppression also hides legitimate test failures that happen to log a message containing that substring via `console.error`. A test that wants to assert an error path was hit by spying on console.error will see nothing because the setup's spy intercepts it first. Consider narrowing further (e.g., require the message to start with the standard React warning prefix) or scoping suppression per-test instead of globally.

afterEach unconditionally restores `__TAURI_INTERNALS__ = {}`, but the comment says the browser-fallback tests `delete` it during their run. If a browser-fallback test fails before it sets up, or if a future test forgets the explicit delete, the reset masks the failure and the next test sees a polluted host. Consider tracking whether the test opted into "pure browser" mode (e.g., a sentinel flag on globalThis) so the reset only fires when the test originally installed `__TAURI_INTERNALS__`.

Defining `__TAURI_INTERNALS__` directly via casted assignment works in jsdom, but in browsers (and jsdom with a locked-down `window`) setting an unknown property on `window` can throw `TypeError: Cannot create property '__TAURI_INTERNALS__': object is not extensible`. Wrap the assignments in a try/catch and log a clear setup warning so the failure mode is obvious, instead of a confusing stack pointing at the test setup.

Prototype-chain safety is honored here (no `Array.prototype`/`Object.prototype` patches), and the comment in the file correctly notes scrollTo/scrollIntoView patches were moved to per-suite scope. No issues found with the rules listed in the checklist — the setup deliberately avoids `eval`, `Function()`, `document.write`, `innerHTML`, and inline style attributes, and uses `const`/`let` exclusively with strict-equality where present.

Critical: `__dirname` is undefined in ESM. The project's `package.json` sets `"type": "module"`, so this `.ts` config is loaded as an ES module where `__dirname` does not exist — vitest will throw `ReferenceError: __dirname is not defined` on startup (e.g. `npm test`). Replace with `import.meta.url`-based resolution: `import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url"; const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));` (or just `path.resolve("./src")` works since vitest's cwd is the config dir, but the ESM-safe pattern is preferable).

Comments explaining the unusual `assetsInlineLimit` SVG rule are written in Chinese. The rationale (the link between test-side SVG import behavior and `?url` matching for `lobe/<slug>` logo assertions) is non-obvious and load-bearing; English (or bilingual) wording would make this easier to debug for non-Chinese contributors and reduce the risk of someone "cleaning up" the option later without realizing why it exists.

The backend `AuditEntry.payload` is `serde_json::Value` and `wa_insert` accepts any JSON value, so the wire payload can be an object, array, string, number, boolean, or `null`. Declaring it as `Record<string, unknown> | null` falsely narrows it to objects/null and hides the fact that downstream code such as `auditPayloadSummary` in `TracePanel` (which does `p.trigger`, `p.total`, etc.) will silently misbehave for any non-object payload that ever lands in the DB. Either widen the TS type to `unknown` (and let consumers narrow), define a JSON value union, or assert/normalize in `listWorkflowAudit`.

Any negative, NaN, Infinity, fractional, or `>2^32-1` value will be rejected at IPC serialization and surface as a generic `Promise` rejection, while `0` is silently bumped to `1`. Enforce the documented contract at the JS boundary instead of leaving validation (and confusing rejections) to the backend.

Negative, NaN, Infinity, fractional, or `>2^32-1` values therefore fail IPC serialization and reject the call with a generic backend error instead of a useful "out of range" message. Validate/normalize at the wrapper boundary to keep the API contract honest.

comments.content: `cancelledRef` is only cleared by a later blur or an explicit commit, but the documented contract lets `onCancel` simply set `editing` false (no blur is guaranteed when React unmounts the focused input). In that case the flag stays true across edit sessions: the next `editing` false→true transition resets the draft and `committedRef`, but `cancelledRef` is still true, so the first real blur of the new edit is treated as the leftover cancellation and `onBlur` returns without committing — the user's edit is silently dropped. Reset `cancelledRef` whenever a new edit session starts (mirror the `committedRef` reset) and, if the input can stay mounted, also when a new user-driven draft change occurs so an Escape stays scoped to the focus that triggered it.

comments.content: Silent error swallowing in respond() — invoke failures are caught and only `console.error`-ed, but the modal is unconditionally cleared in the `finally` (`setPending(p => p === cur ? null : p)`). When `bot_confirm_response` fails, the user sees their click "succeed" (modal closes, buttons re-enable) and believes the dangerous action was confirmed/denied, when in fact the backend never received the decision. The header comment claims backend timeout is the fail-safe, but for an in-flight failure the modal is already gone so the user has no way to retry or be warned. Surface the error to the user (toast, inline error, or keep modal open on failure) so the decision isn't silently dropped.

Stale-closure risk in countdown effect — the effect invokes `respond(false)` on timeout but excludes it from the dependency array via `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`. Today `respond` only reads `pendingRef`/`busyRef` so any version behaves identically, but `respond` is recreated every render and the suppression will silently mask staleness the moment someone adds a closure over `pending` or `busy` state. Either memoize `respond` (wrapped in `useCallback` with stable deps, e.g. `[]`) and include it in deps, or extract the timeout logic into a small helper that takes only the refs/state it needs.

No response on component unmount — the countdown effect only fires `respond(false)` while the component is mounted. If `ConfirmMap` unmounts mid-confirm (route change, hot reload, app shutdown triggered by the very tool being confirmed), the pending `invoke('bot_confirm_response')` is never sent. The header comment and backend 60s timeout cover the happy path, but a failed-shutdown / unmount-during-confirm scenario still leaves the backend oneshot hanging for the full 60s. Add a cleanup that fires `respond(false)` (or at minimum the bare invoke, fire-and-forget) in a `useEffect` cleanup that watches `pending`, so the backend can release the oneshot promptly.

Loose typing for `kind` field — `BotConfirmPayload.kind` is typed as plain `string` with the allowed values documented only in a comment (`"danger" | "file_access" | ...`). The render block then hardcodes equality against `"danger"` and `"file_access"`, which silently degrades to "no badge" for any future kind. Tighten the type to a string union (or enum) so adding a new kind surfaces a type error at the render site rather than a silently missing UI label.

Accessibility gap on a destructive-confirmation modal — the dialog has no `role="dialog"`, no `aria-modal="true"`, no `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby`, no focus trap, and no Escape-key handler. Per the header comment this widget gates EvolutionPanel Promote/Reject/Keep Shadow and other dangerous operations, so a keyboard-only user currently has no way to dismiss it (Escape does nothing, focus is not moved into the modal). At minimum: add `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`, link the title via `aria-labelledby`, set initial focus on the deny button, and bind an Escape key handler to call `respond(false)`.

**Partial-failure leaves inconsistent state**: Three independent `await invoke` calls run sequentially; on a failure after the first success, `proposals` (and possibly `changes`) have already been mutated while the catch sets `error`, so the user sees an "error" banner with partially refreshed data and no rollback of the earlier `setState`. comments.content: FA2 "convergence" detector does not measure motion. The sum is `Math.abs(attrs.x - Math.round(attrs.x)) + Math.abs(attrs.y - Math.round(attrs.y))` — the fractional part of coordinates, not velocity / displacement. As nodes settle they drift toward integer-ish positions and the fractional part collapses regardless of whether motion stopped, so FA2 will be auto-stopped by this metric even when the layout has not actually relaxed, producing uneven/unconverged visuals. Conversely, a layout stuck at integer offsets will see sum=0 from tick 2 onward and be cut off after 5s. Use `Math.hypot(attrs.x - prevX, attrs.y - prevY)` over real velocity attributes (`vx`/`vy`) instead.

comments.content: Mount-only fetch leaves workflow data stale: `workflow_list` is requested exactly once with no listener for workflow changes (unlike `tasks-changed` which refreshes people). If the user adds/edits/deletes a workflow while GraphPage stays mounted, hub counts, filter options, and graph metadata silently drift out of date. Additionally, both `invoke('workflow_list')` and `loadPeople()` only `console.error` on failure — violating the project's "async errors must surface user-friendly messages" rule (users have no way to tell the hub list is incomplete or retry).

People refresh race: every `tasks-changed` event launches a fresh `loadPeople()` with no cancellation token or response-order guard. Rapid successive events (e.g. bulk import) can resolve out of order, so an older snapshot overwrites a newer `people` array — mis-coloring members, breaking the owner/key palette, and producing flicker. The effect itself has no unmount guard either; if the page unmounts while a load is in flight, `setPeople` fires on an unmounted component.

Tag similarity request lifecycle has three correctness/performance problems: (1) `cleanup` only flips a `cancelled` flag — the Rust `tag_similar_pairs` invocation is NOT actually cancelled, so bursts of `tasks` changes spawn many concurrent embedding computations on the backend; (2) on rejection the previous `tagGroups` is left in place (no clear before/after the request), contradicting the comment "引擎不可用 → 无近义"; (3) `tagList` is `useMemo`'d on `tasks` reference identity, so any parent re-render that hands a new array (even with identical tag content) restarts a full-vocabulary request.

Dependency writes are snapshot-based and fire-and-forget: `addDependency`/`removeDependency` derive the new `dependsOn` from `selectedNode?.task` (a closed-over render snapshot) and call the void `onPatchTask` without awaiting/rollback/error surface. Fast successive clicks or parent-side asynchronous patch handling let the second click overwrite the first's payload, silently dropping a dependency; a rejected `task_patch` never surfaces to the user and the editor stays out of sync with backend state. There is also no use of the functional setter form, so multiple queued writes within one render batch all read the same stale `dependsOn`.

Selection-scoped editor state leaks across tasks: `depSearch` and `depError` are never reset when `selectedId` changes. Picking task A, typing a query, then selecting task B keeps A's query (and narrows B's `depCandidates` to nonsense); a "会造成循环依赖" error from A is shown for B and can persist until the user types again. There is no `useEffect` clearing these on `selectedId` (or on `selectedNode`) change.

comments.content: `tabIndex={-1}` only keeps options out of the Tab order — it does NOT prevent focus from moving onto an option when it is clicked (browser default for mousedown). The inline comment claims "焦点保持在触发钮", but on click focus does move to the option, leaving the trigger unfocused until `commit()` synchronously refocuses it. During that gap, the root div's onKeyDown still navigates while `aria-activedescendant` points at the (no-longer-focused) trigger — breaking the activedescendant pattern. Add `onMouseDown={(e) => e.preventDefault()}` to each option (and ideally the listbox container) so mousedown cannot steal focus.

`new Date(report.ts).toLocaleString()` will render "Invalid Date" if the backend ever returns a missing or non-numeric `ts` (e.g. older reports, schema change, malformed payload). The whole "上次执行（…）" line becomes unusable in that case. Validate `report.ts` (e.g. `Number.isFinite(report.ts)`) and fall back to a placeholder like "未知时间" instead of letting the broken date bubble into the UI.

The 5-second `setTimeout` is scheduled unconditionally, even when `path` is empty/falsy (so no notice was actually set). In that case the timer still fires and clears any previously displayed notice (from an earlier action), which is misleading. Move the `setTimeout` inside the `if (path)` branch so it only schedules a clear when a notice was actually shown.

The timer IDs returned by `setTimeout` in `downloadTemplate` and `importRules` are discarded, so the component cannot cancel them. Two real consequences: (a) on unmount during the 3–5s window, React calls `setNotice("")` on an unmounted component (warns on older React, leak on any); (b) rapid successive imports/downloads leave stale timers alive that will clobber newer notices with empty string. Store the IDs in a ref and clear the previous timer before scheduling a new one, and add a `useEffect` cleanup to clear on unmount.

`refresh` is recreated on every render (it's a plain `async const` in the function body), and the mount effect suppresses `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` to call it once. The dependency suppression is a code smell that hides future staleness bugs: if anyone later adds closure state to `refresh` (e.g. a filter, a selected rule id), the mount call will keep reading stale values while the lint stays silent. Wrap `refresh` in `useCallback` with `[]` deps (only setState setters are used) and drop the `eslint-disable`.

The `if (running) return` guard in `runNow` is currently dead: `window.confirm` is synchronous and blocks the event loop, so by the time it returns no second click can be in flight, and the button is already `disabled={running}` for the next render. Worse, the order `confirm → if(running) → setRunning(true)` reads `running` from the closure before the state update lands, which is harmless today but silently breaks if the confirm is ever replaced with an async modal — and `migration_run` is destructive (move/delete user files), so double-invocation is high-blast-radius. Either drop the redundant closure check, or flip the order to `setRunning(true)` first and rely on `disabled` for re-entry protection.

Inline-vs-block detection via position line count is unreliable. CommonMark allows code spans to contain line endings (normalized to spaces), so a multi-line `` `https://...\nfoo` `` inline code span will be classified as a block (isBlock=true) and skip linkification. Conversely, a one-line 4-space indented code block has start.line === end.line and will be treated as inline — if its text is a URL or path, openTarget will be invoked on content that was never meant to be a link. The comment "inline code doesn't span lines" is factually wrong per the CommonMark spec. Consider using `node.tagName` (via the `inline`/`block` distinction from remark) or checking the parent node type instead.

Inline-code linkification bypasses react-markdown's normal URL sanitization pipeline. The rendered `<code>` text is routed straight to `openTarget` via `isHttpUrl`/`isAbsPath` helpers — any model output that happens to be a string recognized by those helpers (e.g. `https://...`, `/etc/passwd`, `\\server\share`, possibly `//evil.com` depending on the helper) becomes a clickable action. Because this is untrusted assistant text, confirm that `isHttpUrl` strictly rejects non-http(s) schemes (javascript:, data:, file:, vbscript:) and that `isAbsPath` does not match UNC, protocol-relative URLs, or other ambiguous forms that could escape to an unintended handler in `openTarget`. Also consider whether remote Markdown images should be allowed — there is no `img` override, so arbitrary image URLs from the model will trigger browser requests (privacy/tracking).

The anchor rendering logic in the `code` branch (href/role/tabIndex/title/className/onClick/onKeyDown + `activate` closure) is duplicated almost verbatim in the `a` branch below. Extract a single helper component (e.g. `OpenTargetLink`) that takes `{ isUrl, href, title, children }` so future security/UX changes (e.g. adding `rel="noopener"`, supporting Space key, fixing modifier-click semantics) only need to be made in one place — otherwise the two paths will silently diverge.

Second copy of the same `<a>` + activate pattern from the `code` branch — same fix applies. Beyond duplication, this branch also drops every other prop that react-markdown may attach to link nodes (e.g. `title`, `rel`, `target`) because the signature only destructures `href` and `children`. If any future Markdown link legitimately carries a `rel` (e.g. `rel="nofollow"` from source) it will be silently discarded here.

`openTarget` is invoked without observing its result. `e.preventDefault()` has already suppressed the native navigation, so if `openTarget` returns a rejected promise or throws, the user sees a dead link with no browser fallback. Even if `openTarget` is expected to surface failures via a popup (per the file-level comment), this contract is not enforced anywhere in this file. Wrap `activate()` in a try/catch (or `.catch(...)` if async) that re-enables native navigation or surfaces an error, so a transient backend failure doesn't silently break clicking.

Left-click handler unconditionally calls `e.preventDefault()` regardless of modifier keys. For URL links this means Ctrl/Cmd-click, Shift-click, and middle-click no longer trigger the browser's native "open in new tab/window" or "open in new window" behavior — they all funnel into `openTarget` and open in the default browser. Either (a) only `preventDefault` when no modifier is held and `e.button === 0`, letting the native handler open the new tab, or (b) explicitly call `openTarget` with the right mode and document this as intentional UX. Path links with no `href` already have no native fallback for middle-click — consider handling `onAuxClick` too.

Keyboard activation only handles `Enter`. Per WAI-ARIA, an element with `role="link"` (which is used here for path links because they have no `href`) is conventionally activatable by both Enter and Space. Add an `e.key === " "` (Space) branch — or omit `role="link"` and use `role="button"` if Space-only is acceptable — so keyboard-only users can actually trigger the file open.

comments.content: Accessibility contract is entirely delegated to the caller, with no guardrail. The header comment correctly notes that `attributes` (role/tabIndex/aria-roledescription/aria-pressed/aria-disabled/aria-describedby) AND `listeners` (KeyboardSensor activation) must both be spread onto the SAME focusable element for keyboard drag to work. Nothing here enforces or warns about that; if a future caller forgets to spread `attributes`, or splits the two onto different elements, keyboard drag silently breaks with no a11y signal. At minimum, add a `propTypes`-style runtime dev warning (e.g. when `listeners` is present but the rendered children DOM does not include the handle props on a focusable element), or document the contract loudly in a JSDoc on the `children` prop so misuse is obvious at the call site.

`handleProps` flips between a fully-populated object and `undefined` depending on whether `listeners` is truthy (e.g. when the item is disabled or no sensor is active). The render-prop consumer must defensively handle the `undefined` branch or the handle will render empty/missing. This is an easy source of subtle a11y regressions where the drag handle "disappears" only in certain states. Either (a) always pass an object (with `attributes` only when `listeners` is absent, signalling "not draggable" via `aria-disabled` rather than removal), or (b) document the `undefined` contract explicitly in the `children` JSDoc and add a typed exhaustiveness check so the caller is forced to handle it.

So after the user clicks the pencil on an answered row, that row stays expanded for the rest of the session even if they then type a fresh answer, change a chip, or clear it via the X button (which also forgets to reset `editing`). The pencil button needs a "done / collapse" path, or `collapsed` should be recomputed from a single derived flag rather than a one-way latch.

comments.content: Re-entrancy hazard: if a second pointerdown fires before the first drag's pointerup (or before its async `startPos` resolves), every call stacks another set of pointermove/up/cancel listeners on `window` while only overwriting `dragCleanupRef.current`. The previous listeners and its `cleanup` closure become orphaned (never removed), pointer capture on the first `el` is never released, and `setWidgetDragActive` is a non-balanced boolean — when the first drag's cleanup finally runs it flips the global flag to `false` even though the second drag is still active, breaking the drag-active invariant downstream. Guard the start of `onDown` by checking `dragCleanupRef.current` (or a "dragging" ref) and call/clear the previous cleanup before registering new listeners; also make `setWidgetDragActive` reference-counted.

Silent drag failure: if `Promise.all` rejects, `startPos` stays `null`, the listeners are still attached, the user drags the edge, and nothing happens — only a `console.warn` is emitted. The component should either fail-fast (call `cleanup` immediately on rejection so the listeners are torn down and `setWidgetDragActive` is reset) or surface the error via UI. Also note the `void Promise.all(...)` has no cancellation token, so a slow resolve after `pointerup` will still assign `startPos` that is then never read.

Unit mismatch risk: `outerPosition`/`outerSize` are divided by `scaleFactor` to get logical pixels, but `ss.w`/`ss.h` from `./storage`'s `screenSize()` are mixed in without a documented unit. If `screenSize()` returns physical pixels (the common case on Windows/macOS Tauri), the resulting `sw`/`sh` will be `sc`× too large and any downstream screen-bounds clamping inside `onDelta` will be wrong by the device pixel ratio. Verify the unit contract of `screenSize()` and either pass it through `sc` or store/document that it is logical.

Code smell / wasted latency: `./storage` is already statically imported at the top of the file (`setWidgetDragActive`), yet `screenSize()` is re-fetched via a dynamic `import("./storage")` on every pointerdown. The dynamic import is either redundant dead-code duplication or hides a real loading concern that should be expressed explicitly. Use the already-imported binding directly so the hot path is one less awaitable and the module graph stays consistent.

comments.content: Combining `setPointerCapture` with window-level pointer listeners is redundant and slightly surprising: window listeners will already receive bubbled events, and pointer capture also forces them through the captured element first. Pick one approach for clarity — either rely on capture (and listen on `el`) or rely on window-level listeners (drop the `setPointerCapture`/`releasePointerCapture` calls and the try/catch scaffolding). Also note that `useEffect`/`useDragCleanup` ordering is not shown here; ensure the hook's unmount handler truly nulls and removes listeners synchronously, otherwise a mid-drag unmount can leave dangling listeners invoking `onSplit` on torn-down parent state.

Render-phase ref write: `expandedRef.current = expanded` is mutated during render (oxlint disabled). This breaks React's render-purity contract and can desync under React 18 concurrent rendering / StrictMode double-invoke, undermining the very "same-tick latest" guarantee the comment claims. Move the assignment into a `useEffect([expanded])` (or use the `useEvent` / `useSyncExternalStore`-style ref pattern) so listeners always read the latest committed value without leaning on a render-side mutation.

Stale closure in `expandFnRef` / no-deps effect pattern: `expandFnRef.current = expand` runs after every render, but `expand` closes over React state (`size.w`/`size.h`/`botOn`). Between a resize commit (e.g. user drags a resize edge) and the next effect flush, `chat-focus-session` will dispatch the previous `expand` with the previous `size`, producing an incorrect window width. Mirror `size`/`botOn` into refs and read them inside `expand`, or memoize `expand` against `size`/`botOn` and refresh the ref via a `[size, botOn]`-keyed effect.

comments.content: Optimistic state is never reverted on `upsertWorkspaceItems` failure. `setItems(next)` runs before the await, and the `catch` only swallows the rejection. A failed write leaves the UI diverged from the DB until the next reload, and subsequent `persist` calls use the optimistic `items` as their base, compounding the divergence (failed changes get re-saved alongside new ones). Either revert on failure, or roll back via a `setItems((prev) => previous)` snapshot captured before the optimistic update.

Rapid double-clicks on "新建工作区" race against the stale closure of `items`. `persist` calls `setItems(next)` synchronously but React doesn't re-render until the next tick, so a second `addItem()` invoked immediately after the first still reads the pre-update `items` from closure and computes the same `max + 1` order. Both items get the same `order`, and the second `persist([...items, D])` makes the first item C disappear from state (it may or may not survive depending on storage semantics). Compute the new order/max inside the functional updater or inside `persist` itself.

`commitEditLink` never recomputes `kind` from the edited `targetUri`, unlike `commitAddLink` which falls back to `"file"` via `looksLikeUrl`. Editing a `"url"` link to point at a local path keeps `kind: "url"`, so `linkDisplayName` returns the full path (no `basename` fallback) and the icon stays `Link2` even though the target is a file. Inconsistent with add-path and produces misleading UI for legacy data with mismatched kind.

Empty `targetUri` in `commitEditLink` silently aborts and discards any `displayName` edit the user made in the same session — the form closes, the link keeps its old targetUri, and there is no feedback that the displayName change was dropped. Either keep the form open and surface the validation error, or at minimum preserve the new displayName by falling back to the existing targetUri while only rejecting an empty target on the original link.

`JSON.stringify` is used for per-item equality in `handleSortEnd`. This is key-order dependent and breaks the moment `WorkspaceItem` gains a non-JSON-safe field (Date, Map, BigInt, `undefined`-vs-missing distinction, Symbol, etc.). It can produce false positives (key reordering across versions) and false negatives (Date values that compare equal but serialize differently). Compare only the fields that `assignInsertOrder` actually touches (e.g., `order`/`updatedAt`) or use a deep-equal helper that understands the schema.

`looksLikeUrl` accepts any RFC-3986-shaped scheme (`javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`, `file:`, `ms-settings:`, ...), not just http(s). Combined with `openTarget(link.targetUri)` being content-driven, a pasted/persisted malicious string can be handed to the OS shell as a non-http scheme. Even if the current Rust backend ignores `javascript:`, the kind inference logic also mis-categorizes these strings as `"url"`, which can corrupt later routing. Tighten to `/^https?:\/\//i` for URL classification and infer `file`/`folder` for anything else (including scheme-bearing paths).

`startsWith` treats any hash beginning with `#/widget` (for example `#/widget-settings` or `#/widget/anything`) as the special window. The Rust entry point currently uses the exact `#/widget` route and no nested widget route is defined, so a user-controlled or malformed hash can mount `WidgetApp` instead of the normal app. Match the complete route or explicitly parse and validate the supported routes.

comments.existing_code: const isWidget = window.location.hash.startsWith("#/widget");

comments.content: Rejections from the security-audit `invoke` are discarded without any diagnostic or fallback. If the Tauri command, permission, or IPC bridge is unavailable, the UI still appears healthy while every CSP violation is lost from the audit trail; the per-session counter has already been consumed, so later events are also suppressed. Keep this non-blocking, but emit a bounded diagnostic or use a fallback and decide explicitly whether failed sends should consume the quota.

This guard does not provide the protection described in the comment. Module-level code is evaluated once per module evaluation, and `React.StrictMode` only remounts components; it cannot cause this top-level block to run twice. If hot module replacement re-evaluates the module, the flag is initialized to `false` again while the previous document listener remains, so it still does not prevent duplicate listeners. Remove the redundant guard, or implement explicit listener disposal for hot reload.

project_summary:
The user wants a project-level summary of a full-repo scan. I need to analyze 1339 comments across 278 files and produce a structured markdown summary with:
1. Top Issues (5-10 most consequential findings)
2. Module Hotspots (directories/modules with high comment density or severity)
3. Cross-Cutting Concerns (patterns appearing across many files)
4. Quick Wins (low-effort, high-leverage fixes)

Let me identify patterns by looking through the comments:

**Top recurring themes I see:**

1. **Mutex poison recovery silently swallowed** - Repeated across MANY files using `e.into_inner()` pattern, especially in bot skills, MCP, chat, scheduler, evolution, memory. This is a massive cross-cutting concern.

2. **UTF-8 / encoding lossy conversions** - `String::from_utf8_lossy` appears in many files (body.rs, migration/commands.rs, mock_llm.rs, etc.) silently replacing invalid bytes with U+FFFD.

3. **String-typed enums instead of proper enums** - In bot/config/types.rs, migration/types.rs, bot/mcp/config.rs, db/tasks.rs, mutation.rs. Free-form strings where enums should exist.

4. **Sync filesystem I/O in async functions** - Blocking std::fs calls in async contexts across many modules (bot/tools.rs, bot_skills/manage.rs, bot_skills/files.rs, migration/commands.rs, py/commands.rs, etc.)

5. **TOCTOU races** - check-then-act patterns everywhere: migration/ops.rs, migration/run.rs, migration/recovery.rs, db/workspace.rs, bot/mcp/keyring.rs, profile.rs, bot_skills/files.rs, intent_router.rs, etc.

6. **Audit logging gaps / error swallowing** - `let _ = ...` pattern across audit calls, audit_log, emit_to. Files like audit.rs, bot/config/audit.rs, bot_artifacts.rs, bot_web.rs, migration/ops.rs.

7. **Cross-cutting JSON/IO error flattening to String** - `.map_err(|e| e.to_string())` and `e.to_string()` losing typed errors across db/*, api_handlers/*, evolution/*, bot/* modules.

8. **DB_WRITE_LOCK contract violations** - bypassed via debug_assert, not enforced, deadlocks.

9. **Secret/token handling weaknesses** - tmp file cleanup, chmod failures, plaintext key migration in api_auth.rs, bot/mcp/secrets.rs, bot/config/io.rs, bot/config/keyring.rs.

10. **Open file / port / IPC TOCTOU** - API start/stop, MCP manager, keyring.

11. **Stringly-typed config / protocol drift** - many "magic string" issues.

12. **Performance issues** - O(n²), unbounded growth, recomputation.

13. **Frontend issues** - React hooks, refs, dependency arrays, nested ternaries (a project rule violation), `useEffect` with refs, missing cleanups.

14. **Tests using `Box::leak`** - Permanent memory leaks in test fixtures.

15. **Script issues** - macOS compatibility, timeouts, TOCTOU, etc.

16. **iOS/macOS/Windows specific concerns** - Bundle suffix case sensitivity, file mode handling, etc.

Let me identify the most impactful findings:

**Top Issues (most consequential):**

1. **SSRF gaps + DNS rebinding in MCP** (bot/mcp/config.rs, bot/mcp/manager.rs) - Public/private check only lexical, no redirect handling, IPv6 coverage incomplete. This is a security-critical area.

2. **MCP unsafe arg execution** (bot/mcp/config.rs) - Allowlist is not execution boundary, env/headers Debug exposes secrets.

3. **Audit log integrity** - `BOT_LOG_LOCK` poisoning recovery, `write_at` re-opens log file every call, chmod failures silently dropped. Critical security trail is broken.

4. **Memory/extraction data loss** - `plan_adjudication` race in memory/extract.rs - two facts can both UPDATE same row, second overwrites first. Cross-key semantic merge in memory/tests.rs destroys source/trust.

12. **Bash scripts lack `set -e`/`set -o pipefail`** and use GNU-only tools (`readlink -f`, `find -maxdepth`, `wc -l < pipe`) — `health-check.sh`, `test-fast.sh`, `install-hooks.sh`, `publish-docx-dotnet.sh`, `fetch_ocr_models.sh`.

## Quick Wins

- **Sweep the `e.into_inner()` pattern.** Across ~25 sites, replace with explicit `lock()?` propagation (returning `CommandError::Lock` or logging then `into_inner()` only when paired with a typed-error pathway). Mechanical change, large reduction in panic-masking.
- **Add `sync_all()` before `renameSync`** in `audit.rs`, `profile.rs`, `paths.rs`, `evolution/{change, candidate}/entry.rs`, `bot/mcp/secrets.rs`, `api_auth.rs`. One-line per site, real durability.
- **Convert free-form Strings to typed enums** (`WorkspaceLink.kind`, `MigrationRule.action`, `JournalEntry.op`, `McpServerConfig.{transport,state}`, `ResolvedModel.api_provider`, `Workspace.enabled` 3-state). Eliminates a class of typo bugs.
- **Stop swallowing `app.emit` / `audit_log` / `log_line`** (`let _ = …` → propagate via `?` or `Result`-returning wrapper) at `db/workflow.rs`, `audit.rs`, `bot/config/audit.rs`, `migration/ops.rs`, `due_notify.rs`, `bot_slash.rs`, `lib.rs`, `migration/run.rs`, `trace_sink.rs`.
- **Stop using `String::from_utf8_lossy` for JSON/structured inputs.** Use `from_utf8(...).map_err(...)` in `body.rs`, `migration/commands.rs` UTF-16 LE/BE, `mock_llm.rs`, and `api_handlers/body.rs`. Cheap and recovers the original error.
- **Replace `let path = String::from_utf16_lossy(...)` with `from_utf16(...)?`** in `migration/commands.rs` (both LE and BE branches) and apply the GBK branch's "fail loud" semantics uniformly.
- **Cap and validate file/path input** in `profile.rs::profile_remove_avatar` (canonicalize + reject `..`, `/`, `\`), `lib.rs::copy_file_with_title` (allow-list or canonicalize under app data), `workspace.rs::workspace_import` (add the same `check_export_path_gate` used by export), `task_autotag.rs` (cap title length in prompt build).
- **In `vite.config.ts`, default `host: false` and require `TAURI_DEV_HOST` to match a CIDR/host allow-list**; lowercase the SVG `endsWith` check; lift `1420/1421` into named constants.
- **Remove `nested ternary` violations across `src/components/`** (a documented project rule).
